title: Understanding Java Release Compatibility
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of understanding java release compatibility and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—source compatibility—in a small, readable example.
Identify one failure, compatibility, security, or resource-management concern and describe a safe response.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study understanding java release compatibility with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you evaluate upgrades using compatibility evidence instead of assuming every release feature is stable. In this lesson, focus on source compatibility and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Java evolves across feature and LTS releases. Review official release notes, deprecations, API compatibility, and preview status before upgrading a project or adopting a new language feature. Apply that reasoning specifically to source compatibility and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect source compatibility with binary compatibility before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.title: Behavioral compatibility
items.text: Use Path and Files for modern file operations, choose byte or character APIs based on the data, and close resources reliably. Parse external files defensively because their contents may be incomplete or malformed.

items.title: Runtime version requirements
items.text: Use the standard library type that matches the data: java.time for dates and zones, BigDecimal for exact decimal arithmetic, and locale-aware APIs for user-facing text and numbers.

items.title: Dependencies on internal APIs
items.text: Primitive variables store values of the eight primitive types. Choose a type that represents the domain and range required; use exact decimal arithmetic for monetary values when appropriate.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Compare source, binary, and behavioral compatibility, then run regression tests against the target JDK. For ordinary Java SE examples, use JDK 25, save a complete class as Main.java, and run `javac Main.java` followed by `java Main`. CodeLeaf does not execute Java in the browser; use a local JDK for these examples. Preview-only and configuration-file examples have their own version or filename notes.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original example, remove any temporary output files it created, and rerun the baseline case. Do not leave credentials, generated private data, or large test files in the project directory.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.

common_mistakes.problem: Applying the rule from memory without checking its exact contract.
common_mistakes.why: Small differences in type, scope, API version, or input shape can change the result.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the relevant official API/language documentation and build a minimal reproducer.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing only a single happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Boundary values and failures often reveal assumptions hidden by the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add an empty, boundary, or invalid case and state the expected behavior before running it.

common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify the actual cause of a different result.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one factor at a time and keep a short record of observed behavior.

Use official versioned documentation and tests to confirm assumptions before relying on behavior in a larger application.
